title: Automated decision tree for cohort rollbacks with explainable rationale
creator: Aisha Menon
description: Design and implement an automated decision-tree service that evaluates multi-metric regressions during cohorted (A/B and staged) rollouts and triggers safe rollback actions with an explainable rationale. The service will combine sequential statistics, lightweight Bayesian detectors, and example-level attribution to produce both a binary rollback decision and a short explanation (metric contributors + representative examples) for SRE/PM/FE review and audit logs. This aims to reduce manual guardrail toil and speed safe reversion while preserving developer trust via transparent reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: Service consumes per-cohort metric streams (quality metrics, latency, cost) and produces a decision: CONTINUE / PAUSE / ROLLBACK with an explanation payload
Automated rollback triggers follow a documented decision tree that includes SPRT-based early stopping plus a Bayesian change-point confirmation to reduce false-positives
Explanation payload contains top 3 contributing metrics, delta values, example-level snippets (1-3) and a short natural-language rationale suitable for Slack/Console alerts
Action executions (feature flag toggle, traffic shift to fallback model variant, or scale-down) are recorded with trace IDs and can be audited via Console and runbook
End-to-end tests simulate regressions and confirm the service triggers rollback in >=95% of injected regressions and <=5% false positives on noise-only signals
implementation_notes: Metric inputs: acceptance_rate, semantic_similarity (embedding-based), hallucination_rate (coverage heuristics), toxicity_score, latency_p95, token_cost_per_request

Decision flow: 1) lightweight detector (SPRT) for fast signal; 2) Bayesian change-point trigger for confirmation; 3) attribution step that ranks metric contributors and surfaces top examples; 4) final decision via deterministic decision tree with hysteresis and cooldown
Statistical safeguards: use sequential p-value correction (alpha spending) and FDR controls across cohorts; require minimum sample sizes per cohort before final ROLLBACK
Explainability: compute SHAP-like metric contributions (simple additive ranking) and select counterfactual/anchor examples using golden prompts from eval-suite

Actions: feature_flag rollback, route traffic to fallback model_family (e.g., quantized variant), or pause rollout (throttle to 0% growth). All actions run through the existing rollout controller API (runtime/rollout?).
Telemetry: log decision_reason, decision_score, evidence_metrics, example_ids, and linkage to the evaluation job so the Console can render interactive traces
RBAC: only service principal with rollback role may auto-execute for P0 regressions; other cases post to on-call channel with ephemeral approval link
test_plan: Unit tests for SPRT and Bayesian detectors with synthetic data (edge cases: small effect size, slow drift, bursty noise)
Integration test that injects synthetic regression into canary cohort and verifies the action executed and audit stored (use local runtime staging env)
Chaos test where rollback action fails to execute (simulate API error) and verify fallback: pause rollout + alert escalation
Regression test: ensure explainability outputs stable representative examples and do not leak PII (sanitize snippets)
Load test: validate decision service can evaluate 200 concurrent cohort streams with sub-200ms decision latency under normal throughput
rollout_playbook: Stage 1 (beta): run service in observe-only mode for all rollouts for 2 weeks; collect signals and tune thresholds
Stage 2 (pilot): enable auto-PAUSE for cohorts flagged as medium-confidence regressions; require manual confirm for ROLLBACK
Stage 3 (gradual): enable auto-ROLLBACK for high-confidence P0 regressions with automatic rollback action and postmortem creation
Operator steps: review explanation in Console, if action executed, evaluate representative examples and approve or escalate to Eng on-call
Escalation: if rollback succeeded but root cause unknown, open triage ticket using templated postmortem and tag with impacted models/configs
